architecture.audioPolicy: Each 100-tick-or-terminal presentation consumes all authority records; accelerated rendering selects newest critical then newest remaining cues up to a fixed cap.
architecture.lifecycleLongTaskPolicy: Drive, restore, terminal observation, restart, screenshots, final observer drain, and out-of-interval tasks are separately attributed and capped at 50ms; entries are classified by start time even when delivery is delayed.
architecture.sliceGuardPolicy: An explicit slice overrun is re-measured deterministically in a quiescent Node audit (bounded retries); only a reproduced overrun fails, while an unreproduced one is recorded as environment noise.
architecture.presentationPolicy: Input is suspended for each 300-tick segment. Every fixed one-tick simulation slice yields through real RAF; every 100 ticks (or terminal) one complete DOM/audio transaction commits, then exactly one E2 input controller remounts at segment finish.
architecture.restorePolicy: Only a consumed replay prefix may rebase; restored history is not rendered into the audio sink.
architecture.transportNormalization: GH attempts use their 300-tick attempt index; browser E2 uses contiguous accepted command IDs. Byte parity is browser-vs-direct-E2, while attempt records compare normalized semantic commands.
architecture.yieldPolicy: Each fixed simulation slice awaits RAF, then Chrome scheduler.yield() when available, then a second cancellable RAF; unsupported schedulers use the two-RAF policy.
architecture.hostPhaseTiming: Diagnostic-only Node performance.now() spans are recorded separately from Chrome page.performance.now() drive timestamps; these measurements do not change the workload or any cap.
architecture.hostPhaseTimingClock: startedAt and durationMs use the Node perf_hooks performance.now clock; browserStartedAt and browserFinishedAt use the Chrome page performance.now clock and are never compared as absolute timestamps.
